text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — kv-cache cluster: sustained paging + NCCL stalls observed on tp-shard group. Severity: P1. Paging rate > 10x baseline, affected: parts of DedCap pool us-west-2. Page sent to oncall.

jamie (eng-sre): I see continuous-batching rate shot up around 11:03 UTC and kv-cache resident set doubled. paging started when shard 7 went into heavy swap. NCCL errors in the node logs.

max (eng-runtime): grabbing logs from shard coordinator. may be a shard assignment imbalance — one tensor-parallel replica held ~60% of keys.

jamie (eng-sre): tagging @oncall — can you ack and join? I kicked incident channel.

oncall (rota): acked. switching to incident channel. I'm oncall for the next hour, leaving pager duty notes in #eng-oncall.

ops-bot: oncall acknowledged the pager for incident 1961234567.

jamie (eng-sre): quick customer-impact note: small number of requests saw 500/timeout spikes for models served from this kv cache group. Estimated impacted requests < 0.5% of overall traffic but a few enterprise tenants saw latency > 10s.

liz (customer-success): flagged two customers in support with alerts. I'll draft outreach once we have mitigation steps.

max (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: continuous batching heuristics triggered a runaway batching loop for long-tail sequences, combined with uneven tp-shard partitioning causing shard 7 to grow its KV cache. When shard 7 hit memory pressure, it started paging which triggered NCCL retries and eventually stalls.

jamie (eng-sre): mitigation plan (short): 1) disable continuous batching on impacted pool 2) force eviction of oversized kv partitions 3) restart kv cache process on affected nodes to clear NCCl stuck state 4) apply emergency routing to fallback model variant.

tess (eng-ml): we should also reduce batch_window_ms and max_batch_size to avoid immediate re-trigger. Suggest patch: batch_window_ms=25 -> 10, max_batch_size=64 -> 32 for the pool.

max (eng-runtime): performing step 1 now: disabling continuous batching for dedcap-usw2 pool. Command: `rbctl config set pools/dedcap-usw2/continuous_batching false --prod`

jamie (eng-sre): running eviction and restart on the hot nodes. Commands: ```
# evict largest kv partitions
rbctl kv evict --shard tp-7 --keys top-1000 --force
# restart kv worker on node
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart daemonset/kv-worker-node-tp7
```

ops-bot: executed: `rbctl kv evict --shard tp-7 --keys top-1000 --force` — accepted by control plane, job queued.

max (eng-runtime): I see NCCL errors in the node kernel logs: ```
E NCCL 0x7f9d: too many retries, op=allreduce, rank 3 -> abort
E NCCL 0x7f9d: deadlock detected on ring -> resetting communicator
```

jamie (eng-sre): after eviction we observed immediate drop in paging and a sharp decrease in 95th latency. Rolling restart cleared the NCCL hang on two nodes.

tess (eng-ml): pushing hotfix to shard assignment to add a safety cap: if partition > 45% of pool memory then rebalance proactively. hotfix PR opened: `eng-ml/kv-shard/PR#4899`

max (eng-runtime): applying ephemeral routing to divert new requests away from dedcap-usw2->tp-7 until we can roll out hotfix: `rbctl route set pool/dedcap-usw2 fallback=true --duration 30m`

jamie (eng-sre): taking an on-call handoff to @tess in 30m for follow-through on rollout and validation.

liz (customer-success): sending initial courtesy email to impacted customers: "we detected transient latency for requests between 11:03-11:22 UTC caused by internal caching reroute; mitigations are in progress. We'll follow up with RCA."

ops-bot: rollout restart daemonset/kv-worker-node-tp7 completed on 3/4 nodes, node-07 failing with crashloop -> quarantined.

jamie (eng-sre): quarantined node-07 shows repeated driver OOMs; we've isolated it and rebalanced traffic away. continuing to monitor.

max (eng-runtime): hotfix merged and will be rolled to staging first. patch includes: proactive eviction threshold, balanced partitioner, and guard for continuous-batching backoff.

tess (eng-ml): scheduling canary deploy now to dedcap-usw2 small subset (5%). Watchlist: paging rate, NCCL errors, 95th latency, memory RSS per shard.

jamie (eng-sre): canary started at 11:48 UTC. initial results: no paging, no NCCL errors on canary.

liz (customer-success): customers want ETA for full fix — ETA to prod roll is ~40m pending canary success, i'll update tickets.

oncall (rota): handoff note: if paging resumes or NCCL reappears, escalate to eng-runtime and open escalation channel with logs. I will remain reachable.

jamie (eng-sre): post-mitigation status at 12:10 UTC: continuous batching disabled, eviction executed, 3/4 kv workers restarted, traffic diverted, canary healthy. Impact: degraded but contained; no new customer errors after 11:55 UTC.

tess (eng-ml): next actions for follow-up (post-incident): 1) emergency test suite for tp-shard imbalances 2) add automated detector for KV partition skew > 40% 3) tune continuous batching fallback to backoff faster 4) improve runbook for eviction + NCCL resets.

max (eng-runtime): I'll open the RCA draft and include the relevant logs and commands used. planning postmortem timeline: share initial RCA in 24h, final RCA in 72h.

jamie (eng-sre): thanks team. tagging incident as "mitigated" for now, leaving channel open for next 2 hours for observations. :white_check_mark:
